summary.title: Instruction tables: latencies, throughputs and micro-operation breakdowns
summary.one_liner: Agner Fog's reference of measured x86 instruction latencies, reciprocal throughputs, micro-op counts and execution port data for Intel, AMD and VIA CPUs.
takeaways: Latency is the delay an instruction adds to a dependency chain; reciprocal throughput is the average cycles per instruction when instructions are independent.
Figures are the author's measured values under specific conditions, and can differ from vendor-published numbers.
Micro-op counts and execution ports matter when a bottleneck limits μops per cycle or same-port usage.
Memory read/write latency cannot be measured alone; only the combined store-to-load forwarding latency is meaningful.
Tables cover many Intel, AMD and VIA CPUs, from P5 Pentium through Zen 5 and Tiger Lake, with the test processors listed.
summary.summary: This PDF, the fourth of Agner Fog's five optimization manuals (last updated 2025-09-20), defines the terms used in its tables: latency, reciprocal throughput, μops, execution unit and execution port. It explains the measurement method, which uses dependency chains for latency and independent instruction sequences for throughput, plus performance counters where available. It also lists the x86 instruction sets and the list of tested processors from AMD K7 through Zen 5 and Intel Pentium through Tiger Lake. The instruction tables themselves are not included in the page text provided.
